5. He further submits that actually applicant is labour and he is very poor person and due to his bad financial condition deceased remained under depression and due to this reason she committed suicide.

He further submits that immediately after the incident applicant informed the police as well as to the informant and on his information inquest was conducted and at the time of inquest from the side of applicant and informant number of persons were present and subsequently next day FIR of the present case was lodged.
He further submits that post mortem report of the deceased also shows that she died due to hanging.

He further submits that applicant is not having any criminal history and in the present matter he is in jail since 04.12.2022.
6.

Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died within seven years of her marriage under abnormal circumstances in her matrimonial home, therefore, applicant does not deserve bail.
7. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

8. Although, applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died within seven years of her marriage under abnormal circumstances in her matrimonial home but in the FIR there is no allegation of demand of dowry.

9. Further, from the record it reflects that on the information of the applicant, Panchayatnama was conducted and during Panchayatnama even family members of the deceased were also present and FIR of the present case was lodged next day.

10. Further, applicant has taken defence that he is labour and this fact also finds support from the statement of one independent witness Monu Rajpoot and due to his bad financial condition deceased committed suicide.
Further, post mortem report of the deceased also shows that she died due to hanging.

11. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant, who is although husband, is entitled to be released on bail.
12. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

13. Let the applicant - Surendra Rajpoot @ Bangali be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-

sentences.text: (i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
14. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.
